Sara — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to provide everything. Quick high-level answers while we assemble the package: 

- PHI flows: PHI is accepted via TLS-encrypted REST endpoints, passed through our inference runtime with in-memory KV cache; persistent PHI storage is not required for typical inference (we offer configurable retention policies, default: ephemeral). We do offer optional persisted audit logs and customer-configured logging sinks.
- SOC2: we will attach the 2026 SOC 2 Type II summary and provide the full report under NDA.
- KMS: Redwood supports provider-managed KMS by default and offers customer-managed key (BYOK) integrations with AWS KMS & Azure Key Vault in Dedicated/Private deployments. HSM-backed keys are supported for Private deployments.
- BAA: attaching an editable Redwood BAA draft for your team to review; we can take your redlines or propose alternate wording.

We will deliver a consolidated evidence zip by Oct 27 (aiming earlier). Is Oct 30 a hard cutoff for the assessor?

I'll loop in Naomi (security) and David (infrastructure) to pick up the artifacts.

Thanks,
Hannah
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Naomi / Hannah — thanks for the package. A few follow-ups from our review: 

1) The phi-dataflow-diagram callouts are helpful; can you annotate where KV cache contents may contain temporary PHI and how cache eviction and purging are triggered?
2) For the KMS note: please expand on key access controls (who at Redwood has the ability to decrypt customer data when customer-managed keys are in use?).
3) The BAA has a section on breach notification timelines — CardioNova requires a 24-hour notification window for ePHI incidents; would Redwood accept that timeframe in a redline?

We may request a short screen-share next week to validate runtime behavior and purge paths.

— CipherTrust Security Review (on behalf of CardioNova)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Thompson <sara.thompson@cardionova.com>, sec.consult@ciphertrust.io <sec.consult@ciphertrust.io>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: PHI dataflow + evidence for HIPAA review

Thanks — quick answers and next steps: 

1) KV cache: temporary PHI can exist in the in-memory KV cache during a live session. Eviction policy is LRU with configurable TTL per deployment; for sensitive integrations we can reduce TTL to zero (no caching) and enable synchronous purging on session end. We'll annotate the diagram and add a short log of purge API calls.

2) KMS access: in BYOK modes where customer-provided keys are used, Redwood does not hold key material. For provider-managed keys we enforce role-based access: only a limited set of runops engineers can request decryption via an audited process; all such operations require two-person review and generate immutable audit logs. We'll expand the encryption-kms-brief.md to include role names, audit log examples, and rotation cadence.

3) 24-hour breach notification: legal is looped in via Marissa and will review the requested timeline. From a technical/ops standpoint we can support escalating telemetry and runbooks to meet a 24-hour notification SLA where feasible; final acceptance requires legal sign-off on incident scope and remediation obligations.

Proposed next steps: Marissa will prep a BAA redline (editable) and Naomi will produce an annotated dataflow and purge-demo script. Can we schedule a 45-minute walkthrough with CipherTrust next Wed (Oct 27) at 10am PT? Sara — does that work for you?

Thanks,
Hannah
